681-program-description: One year preparing you for an OMFS residency: assisting residents with patient care, plus lectures, seminars and journal clubs. One or two places, for Canadians or PRs from accredited North American schools, or sponsored programs.
681-program-description-2: Four years from July 1, accredited, with an optional M.Sc. year, for practising and academic surgeons. Only for graduates of sponsored programs. Needs a D.D.S. or D.M.D., a limited ODQ licence (no French test first), a year of internship or GPR, and ACLS.
681-program-description-3: Six years from July 1, accredited, with an M.D.,C.M. Only for dentists who are Canadian or PR, from accredited North American schools, with a limited ODQ licence.
683-graduate-and-postgraduate-dentistry-: Some are in the Professional section; others in the graduate section.
683-continuing-dental-education: Recognized by licensing bodies, in clinical and basic sciences, to keep practitioners and researchers current. See the page for the list.
684-faculty-of-education: Over a century preparing education professionals, advancing knowledge and practice in Québec, Canada and internationally.
684-department-of-integrated-studies-in-: Prepares elementary and secondary teachers: four-year B.Ed. for CEGEP graduates, five years for out-of-province, and options with prior degrees.

B.Ed. in Secondary English, Math, Science and Technology, Social Sciences; Kindergarten and Elementary, with First Nations and Inuit, Jewish Studies or French Immersion; TESL. B.Mus./B.Ed. isn't currently offered. B.A.(Education) in Global Contexts, and First Nations and Inuit programs (p. 699).
684-department-of-educational-and-counse: Research on cognition and development across the lifespan, assessment and intervention, neuroscience, and learning environments. Minor concentrations (p. 697).
684-department-of-kinesiology-and-physic: Knowledge about health and physical activity, and professional preparation. B.Ed. in Physical and Health Education, B.Sc. Kinesiology Major and Honours, and a B.Sc. minor (p. 738).
684-overview-of-programs-offered: Undergraduate: B.Ed., which can lead to certification, B.A. in Education, B.Sc. in Kinesiology. Professional development for teachers: certificates and diplomas, mostly evenings and summer. Graduate: master's and doctorates, and a Master of Arts in Teaching and Learning with certification.
685-programs-for-first-nations-and-inuit: For First Nations and Inuit teachers, through OFNIE, Education Building, Room 431A. One route to certification, plus Student Personnel Services (p. 734) and Inclusive Education (p. 737) for certified teachers, with enrolment limits.
685-programs-of-professional-development: Usually 30 credits, part-time possible, normally for certified teachers.
685-programs-offered: Certificate in Inclusive Education; Diploma in Human Relationships, Diversity and Sexuality. Room 614.
685-programs-offered-2: Graduate Certificates in Educational Leadership and TESL. Room 244.
685-the-office-of-first-nations-and-inui: With Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, the Cree School Board, Kahnawà:ke Education Centre and other Indigenous communities, delivers field-based programs leading to certification and B.Ed. degrees, at McGill or off campus.
686-undergraduate-education-programs: All B.Ed. programs are CAPFE-accredited. CEGEP gives 30 credits of Advanced Standing, sometimes fewer. Without CEGEP, French or IB, or a university year, add a 30-credit Foundation: 120 for B.A.(Ed.) and B.Sc.(Kin.), 150 or 167 for B.Ed.
686-bachelor-of-education-programs-leadi: Completing a program, plus Ministry requirements, means recommendation for Québec certification. The concurrent Music program isn't currently offered.
686-bachelor-of-arts-and-bachelor-of-sci: B.A.(Education), Global Contexts (90 credits): education for global challenges across sociology, psychology, leadership, history and policy, with a semester internship, for non-classroom educators.
B.Sc. Kinesiology (90 credits): human movement from social, historical, psychological and biological angles, with minors and an Honours for graduate-bound students.
686-general-admission-requirements: See the Undergraduate Admissions Guide. Secondary Science, Secondary Math and Kinesiology have math or science prerequisites. For transfers and readmission, see p. 39, p. 41 and the ISA site.
687-language-requirement-for-applicants-: Apply to McGill; those considered may need to pass written and oral English tests.
687-credit-requirements: B.Ed. 120 credits, or 150 with Foundation; B.A.(Ed.) and B.Sc.(Kin.) 90, or 120. At least 60 at McGill.

Transfer credit is decided after you apply. Courses over five years old aren't allowed where content changed, nor pedagogy for Québec's K-11; others go to the Program Director. Check your record, and see your adviser in your admitted term.
687-language-proficiency: Oral and written fluency in the language of instruction is required for certification.
687-confidential-declaration-concerning-: Under a 2005 Québec law, anyone seeking certification must submit a confidential judicial record declaration to the Minister.
687-quebec-teacher-certification: The Ministry certifies, on McGill's recommendation, and you must apply. All B.Ed. graduates can apply for a permanent Brevet at graduation, by the deadline.
To teach elsewhere, get Québec certification first and check that place's rules. Those from elsewhere apply to the Ministry.
687-international-students: You need a co-op or internship work permit, besides CAQ and study permit, with a medical exam by a designated physician, or you can't work in schools or start your placement. For a Brevet, hold a Post-Graduation Work Permit or study permit.
688-faculty-regulations-for-undergraduat: University rules apply, plus these. Correct courses, requirements, deadlines and records are your responsibility.
688-advising: Internships and Student Affairs (ISA), Education Building, Room 243.
688-academic-advising: New students must see an adviser before Fall. Returning students are advised in spring. Those entering their final year should meet their program adviser.
688-academic-standing: Based mainly on CGPA and TGPA, and for B.Ed. on Field Experience. Fall decisions are Interim and advisory.
An F in a Fall EDFE means Unsatisfactory, though the ISA Director may allow Winter courses. A D means Probationary.
688-interim-probationary-standing-at-the: Continue, reduce your load, and see your adviser before withdrawal deadlines. First- or Second-Year Field Experiences may proceed.
688-probationary-standing-at-the-end-of-: Continue with at most 12 credits, no Field Experience next year, raise TGPA and CGPA, and see your adviser.
688-placement-in-probationary-standing: CGPA 1.50–1.99 after Satisfactory; a D in Field Experience after Satisfactory; CGPA 1.50–1.99 and TGPA 2.50+ after Probationary or Interim Unsatisfactory; or the same after Readmitted, meeting your letter's conditions.
689-interim-unsatisfactory-standing-at-t: Continue, reduce your load and see an adviser, but no next Field Experience (B.Ed.) or internship (B.A.).
689-unsatisfactory-standing: You've missed the minimum standards and can't continue, or do planned internships or field experience.
689-placement-in-unsatisfactory-standing: CGPA below 1.50; TGPA under 2.50 with CGPA under 2.00 after Probationary, Readmitted or Interim Unsatisfactory; failure (F, J, KF, WF) in any Field Experience, in any term; or missing your readmission conditions.
Concurrent B.Mus./B.Ed.: F or J in Field Experience means leaving that program, though you can ask Schulich about a B.Mus.
689-readmission: Apply in Minerva by July 1 (Fall) or November 15 (Winter). Appeal to the ISA Director with proof of extenuating circumstances. A second Unsatisfactory means leaving permanently.
After a Field Experience failure, wait at least a full year, apply by April 15 for Fall, and the Student Affairs Committee hears the appeal.
689-readmission-after-unsatisfactory-sta: You become Readmitted Unsatisfactory, with a set load and conditions. See your adviser.
689-incomplete-standing: Clear Ks, Ls or supplementals. You can register for Fall, but it must be settled by the end of course change.
You continue if it becomes Satisfactory, Probationary or Interim Unsatisfactory. If Unsatisfactory, ask the Director right away, with proof. If still Incomplete, contact ISA.
689-attendance: Varies by course, and is critical in B.Ed. for professional competence. Unexcused absences can mean exclusion, failure or removal from a Field Experience.
Field Experience needs punctuality throughout. Some start in August, some are in spring or overlap exams, so check the schedule; you're excused for a final exam. See the Student Teaching e-Handbook.
690-course-load: Usually 15 credits a term; under 12 is part-time. Satisfactory: up to 17. CGPA above 3.00: may ask for more, not in major Field Experience terms. Probationary: at most 12.
B.Ed. and B.Sc.(Kin.) are full-time only, unless the ISA Director agrees before add/drop ends. B.A.(Ed.) can be part-time within the time limit.
690-part-time-student-status: Not allowed in order to study elsewhere. It can affect your time limit, scholarships, loans, aid, awards, immigration, insurance, and student discounts such as OPUS. Keep documents justifying it, and check with the relevant office first.
690-time-limit-and-credits-for-completio: B.Ed.: five years and 150 credits. B.A.(Ed.) and B.Sc.(Kin.): four years and 120. Foundation students start counting after a year. Going beyond takes permission, for valid academic reasons, and only needed courses count.
690-course-requirements: C or better in program courses. If short, pass a supplemental or repeat, or replace a complementary. See your adviser yearly, and at the end of year 3 (B.Ed.) or 2 (others). Failure in Field Experience means leaving the program.
691-electives: Any McGill course, except Continuing Studies courses with C codes (CHEM excepted). See below for online.
691-courses-taken-as-transfer-credit: Outside Québec: approval from your adviser and ISA first, only for courses your program needs, and not in your graduating term.
691-inter-university-transfer-credit: 3, exceptionally 6, credits a term in Québec, with your adviser's permission. Only needed courses, and not in your graduating term.
691-online-courses: At most 18 credits, with approval for other universities' courses. May affect some government loans.
691-courses-taken-under-satisfactory-uns: Not for required or complementary courses, including B.Ed. subject courses.
691-course-equivalencies-and-overlap: No extra credit for overlaps. Know the exclusions, and confirm Advanced Standing and exemptions.
691-dress-code-regulations: Follow school rules on attire. Kinesiology and Physical Education need suitable activity clothing and possibly some equipment.
691-english-language-requirement: B.Ed. students write the English Exam for Teacher Certification in their first semester (Foundation in Year 1), and must pass before the Fourth Field Experience. Register for EDEC 215 and with CEETC, and pay each time.
Failing means support and a retake. After five tries, ask the ISA Director. A sixth failure means withdrawal. Not for First Nations and Inuit certificates.
692-examinations: See p. 62. Tentative schedule about a month in, final about two. Don't book travel early.
692-supplemental-examinations: Apply in Minerva by the deadline, in Satisfactory or Probationary Standing with D, J, F or U.
692-reassessment-and-rereads: You can see and discuss your graded work. Two types: reassessing coursework and rereading a final.
692-reassessment-of-course-work: Ask within 10 working days of its return, normally done within 20. The reviewer judges fairness. The grade can go up or down, and the new one stands.
692-rereads-of-final-exams-or-final-term: Write to ISA by March 31 (Fall), June 30 (Winter) or September 30 (Summer), strictly. Talk to the instructor first if you can. The grade can change either way. Other faculties' rules apply to their courses.
692-grading: Outlines in the first week describe evaluation. See p. 53 and the assessment policy.
692-graduation-requirements: All requirements, C or better in program courses, CGPA 2.00, and 60 McGill credits. Kinesiology and Physical Education need First Aid and CPR Level C by final year.

Within five years (B.Ed.) or four (others); B.Ed. for Certified Teachers, 12. Check with your adviser early, apply in Minerva, and complete certification forms. Tell ISA of any date change. No outside courses in your last term.
693-incomplete-grades: K with a date. Limits: April 30 (Fall), July 30 (Winter), November 15 (Summer). Instructors may set earlier ones, especially if you're graduating.
693-judicial-record-verification-for-stu: School boards may check anyone in regular contact with minors, including student teachers. Without clearance you can't do Field Experience and must leave the program.
693-mcgill-principles-of-practice-behavi: Teacher candidates should be knowledgeable, flexible, compassionate and socially responsible. The whole community is expected to act professionally and accountably, and to respect everyone regardless of sex, orientation, gender, race, religion, language, age or ability.
Graduates must meet Québec's Professional Teacher Competencies. Read the full document.
693-registration-and-withdrawal: Register in Minerva. Unsatisfactory at year end cancels registration, unless the Director readmits you. Unpaid fees or fines block registration; see Student Aid. If not returning, withdraw in Minerva or file the form.
694-course-registration: Follow your program overview. Some courses need permission, so check early. Prerequisite waivers must be written by an adviser.
694-course-withdrawal: Three periods, on Important Dates. Exceptionally later, with the Late Course Withdrawal form and documents.
694-dean-s-honour-list-designation-for-g: Top 10% of graduates, with 60+ McGill credits, by CGPA.
694-dean-s-honour-list-designation-for-i: Top 10%, with 27+ graded credits that year, by sessional GPA.
694-scholarships-and-awards: Open to graduating and continuing students. See the aid and ISA sites.
694-student-teaching-field-experience: ISA arranges placement and evaluation of student teachers.
694-about-field-experiences: Required EDFE courses from first to fourth year, in sequence. Never arrange your own placement. Mostly in English boards or private schools in Québec; TESL in Francophone ones. Budget travel. They may run past lectures, through breaks, and into May.
694-registration-for-the-student-teachin: Register by the date emailed to your McGill address, and submit the Placement Form on time. Don't take conflicting courses.

Returning students need Satisfactory Standing and all prerequisites. Secondary needs 24 subject credits before FE3. All need the EETC before FE4. Minerva may not stop you, and you'd be removed. Transfers among K/Elementary, Secondary and TESL needn't repeat FE1.
695-student-responsibilities: Know the rules, and avoid jobs or conflicting courses during placements.
695-guidelines-syllabus: Guidelines and forms are on the ISA site by program and year.
695-attendance-and-absences: Be on time throughout, with no alternate dates. Illness and McGill exam days are made up; over four days needs a medical note. Tell your Cooperating Teacher, Placement Coordinator (with the form) and Supervisor that morning.
Religious observance: notify all before it starts, and make up the days. Intercollegiate sport: form two weeks ahead. Others: exceptional, two weeks' notice.
695-work-permit-for-international-studen: A free internship or co-op permit, separate from a study permit, needing a medical exam at varying cost. It takes time, so ask ISS.
695-grading-and-credit: Pass or Fail from Supervisor and Cooperating Teacher reports. Serious difficulties with potential may get a D, and one repeat, by the ISA Director.
D, F or W means withdrawing from and repeating the corequisite seminar. You need P to proceed. Failure means Unsatisfactory and leaving. Appeal to the Student Affairs Committee.
696-early-dismissal-from-field-experienc: Your host or ISA can remove you for missing prerequisites, too many absences, failing a record check, unprofessional behaviour or not showing competencies. The Director decides: reassignment, W, D (one repeat, on Probation), or failure and leaving. The same applies if you end it yourself.
696-withdrawal-from-field-experience: For a refund, notify ISA in writing and deregister at least two weeks before. Later or mid-placement, tell ISA at once, and the Director decides.
696-transfer-credit: Field Experience from elsewhere doesn't transfer; all must be done at McGill.
697-about-the-department-of-educational-: Learning, cognition, instruction, technology, evaluation, inclusive education and family impact. Runs the B.A. minor (p. 198), professional programs in Human Relationships, Inclusive Education and Counselling Applied to Teaching, and a Psychoeducational and Counselling Clinic.
697-graduate-and-postdoctoral-studies: M.A. in Counselling, Educational (thesis) and School/Applied Child Psychology; M.Ed. in Educational Psychology; Ph.D. in Counselling, School/Applied Child and Educational Psychology.
697-program-description: Relationships in a digital, global world, from an intersectional, social justice view: sexuality, culture, ability, media literacy, communication, advocacy and leadership.
699-about-the-department-of-integrated-s: Formed in September 2001 from four earlier departments. B.Ed. in four years from CEGEP or five otherwise; B.A.(Education) in three or four.
699-secondary-education-b-ed-programs: 120 credits (150 from outside): subject depth with pedagogy, curriculum and foundations around school placements. English, Math, Science and Technology, or Social Sciences. Math and Science have specific requirements.
699-bachelor-of-arts-b-a-education-progr: 90 credits (120 from outside): theory and global issues, for work in government, education, industry and communities. No teacher certification.
699-music-education-music-elementary-and: Not currently offered. B.Mus. and B.Ed. together, normally five years, four with credits. Apply through Schulich. Those with a B.Mus. apply to the B.Ed. in Music with Advanced Standing.
700-kindergarten-and-elementary-educatio: 120 credits (150 from outside): general subjects with pedagogy around placements. Options: First Nations and Inuit Studies, Jewish Studies (Prof. Eric Caplan), and French Immersion.
700-teaching-english-as-a-second-languag: 120 credits (150 from outside) for elementary and secondary ESL, with liberal education, language studies and placements. Pass the English Language Proficiency Test before admission. Option: Teaching Greek Language and Culture.
700-graduate-programs: M.A. in Education and Society, Educational Leadership, and Second Language Education; MATL with secondary certification; graduate certificates in Leadership, TESL and French Immersion.
